options.text: The movement of particles against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration
The movement of particles down a concentration gradient
The random movement of water molecules
The movement of particles that does not require energy

questions.explanation: Active transport is the movement of substances from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration (against the concentration gradient), requiring energy from cellular respiration (ATP).

questions.stem: Where does the energy for active transport come from?

options.text: Diffusion
Sunlight
Cellular respiration (ATP)
Osmosis

questions.explanation: The energy for active transport comes from ATP produced during cellular respiration. This is why cells that carry out a lot of active transport have many mitochondria.

questions.stem: How do root hair cells use active transport?

options.text: To release water into the soil
To absorb light energy
To release carbon dioxide
To absorb mineral ions from the soil against their concentration gradient

questions.explanation: Root hair cells use active transport to absorb mineral ions from the soil, where they are at a lower concentration than inside the cell. This requires energy because it moves ions against the concentration gradient.

questions.stem: How does active transport differ from diffusion?

options.text: Active transport only occurs in plant cells
Active transport moves particles against the concentration gradient and requires energy; diffusion does not
Diffusion requires energy but active transport does not
There is no difference

questions.explanation: Active transport moves substances from low to high concentration (against the gradient) and requires energy from ATP. Diffusion moves substances from high to low concentration (down the gradient) and is passive.

questions.stem: Why do cells involved in active transport have many mitochondria?

options.text: Mitochondria reduce the concentration gradient
Mitochondria produce the ATP needed to power active transport
Mitochondria make the cell membrane more permeable
Mitochondria store the substances being transported

questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration to produce ATP, which provides the energy needed for active transport. Cells with high active transport rates need many mitochondria to meet their energy demands.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of active transport in the human body?

options.text: Oxygen moving from the lungs into the blood
Carbon dioxide diffusing out of cells
Glucose being absorbed from the gut into the blood against a concentration gradient
Water moving into root hair cells

questions.explanation: In the gut, glucose can be absorbed by active transport when its concentration in the blood is already higher than in the gut. This ensures all glucose is absorbed from digested food.

questions.stem: What role do carrier proteins play in active transport?

options.text: They bind to specific molecules and use ATP to move them across the membrane
They break down the substance being transported
They produce ATP for the cell
They dissolve in the cell membrane

questions.explanation: Carrier proteins in the cell membrane bind to specific molecules, change shape using energy from ATP, and move the molecules across the membrane against the concentration gradient.
